hazard.label: Flood - open water seen by radar

observation.sensor_detail: NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band HH, GCOV gamma-0
observation.product: NISAR L2 GCOV, Frequency A, HH polarization
observation.source: NASA-ISRO NISAR, Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) catalogue and data access
observation.method: NISAR L2 GCOV HH gamma-0 linear power converted to dB. Baseline and flood observations are aligned onto a common local UTM grid. A 50 m focal median is applied before the two-date ratio calculation. Permanent water from JRC Global Surface Water occurrence above 50%, slopes of 5 degrees or more, and pixels with baseline brightness at or above -3 dB are excluded. The threshold is selected using the NISAR processor's Otsu method and configured fallback. Morphological opening and an 8-pixel minimum patch filter are applied.
observation.limitations: Experimental NISAR L-band flood classification. The threshold has not been independently calibrated for this event. This method detects open water only. Flooded vegetation, cropland and buildings can produce increased radar backscatter through double-bounce effects and may be missed. The detected flood area is therefore not a complete estimate of inundation.
observation.not_ground_truth: This is a satellite-derived experimental observation, not ground truth. No event-specific independent validation or accuracy figure is claimed.

context.roads_note: A road is flagged when it crosses an area where the radar saw open water on the observation date. That is not a statement that the road is impassable, and an unflagged road is not confirmed open: radar cannot see water under trees or between buildings, and it knows nothing about depth or current.

terrain.source: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA / Airbus), open data on AWS
terrain.method: Window read of the public tiles, merged to UTM, hillshade at azimuth 315 and altitude 45 degrees, 30 m grid
terrain.limitations: A surface model: it includes buildings and trees and it smooths low flat land. It shows the shape of the ground. It is not a flood model.

usage: Prepared while online, then carried into the field. Once this file is on the device the instrument needs no network: no tiles, no services, no accounts.
